source_row.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Defer routine screening until age 60 because average-risk adults younger than 60 do not benefit.","B":"Wait for gastrointestinal symptoms before screening because asymptomatic adults do not meet screening criteria.","C":"Begin colorectal cancer screening now using one of the USPSTF-recommended screening strategies.","D":"Begin annual colonoscopy now because colonoscopy every year is the preferred USPSTF screening strategy."}}
source_row.rationale: USPSTF recommends colorectal cancer screening beginning at age 45 for average-risk asymptomatic adults. Option C is correct. Screening is preventive rather than symptom-triggered, and multiple strategies are acceptable; annual colonoscopy is not the recommended schedule.
source_row.source_detail: Recommendation Summary: screen average-risk asymptomatic adults age 45-49 (Grade B) and age 50-75 (Grade A); selectively offer screening age 76-85 based on health, prior screening, and preferences. USPSTF Final Recommendation Statement dated 2021-05-18; remains the current final USPSTF colorectal-cancer screening recommendation, live-rechecked 2026-08-15. NCSBN first-check: Client Needs — Health Promotion and Maintenance: preventive screening, immunization, pregnancy/reproductive health and age/risk-appropriate teaching activities as applicable. 2026 NCLEX-RN Test Plan; effective 2026-04-01 through 2029-03-31; currentness rechecked 2026-08-15.
source_row.stem: An asymptomatic 45-year-old adult at average risk for colorectal cancer has never been screened. What does the USPSTF recommend?
